terra.problem: Saying everything else in the chapter follows from God's holiness assigns that reason to every command, which the passage does not state.
The verse names mother and father, not necessarily the people who raised the listener.
It supplies a reason for the prohibition on molten gods that the verse does not give.
The shiny side-project joke makes light of making false gods, a serious sin.
The leftover joke makes the peace offering, something holy to the LORD, the subject of the joke.
Calling provision for people in need the whole point of the command adds a purpose the text does not state and reduces the named recipients to that description.
God seeing the act is a Bible fact not stated in this passage and needs a supporting reference.
The extra-credit joke uses a school comparison, which is outside the audience rules.
Slander does not mean all words that hurt a neighbor; the definition is too broad.
After the quotation, the explanation merely restates that slander is prohibited and notes the closing words. It is noticeably generic.
Direct rebuke is made specifically face to face, and the explanation claims hatred and a conversation cannot coexist. The verse says neither.
The explanation repeats the verse and says it is in the text without adding an explanation or distinctive voice.
After quoting the verse, the explanation only says that God said it and repeats the closing words. It is flat and generic.
The explanation repeats both that there is no fine and that the outcome is defilement without adding anything of substance.
Saying rising and honoring are all the verse asks overlooks its command to fear God.
